fullPassage: In his exploration of how we engage with language, John Stuart Mill noted that there is a distinction between the denotation and connotation of words. The denotation of a word is its basic, dictionary definition —the straightforward umbrella term for any entity. For example, the term “human” denotes a person and can be used to refer to all human beings —Alice, Bill, and countless other individuals. To put it another way, denotation is the broad category of actual referents to which a word can be applied. Connotation, on the other hand, is more complicated as it encompasses all the additional attributes and contexts a word can carry that may not be part of its explicit definition. The term “human,” according to Mill, embodies characteristics such as corporeality, biological life, the ability to reason, and a specific external form, and these are what make the word “human” applicable to all the individuals. In essence, grasping the connotation of a word means having a nuanced understanding of the entity the word refers to. By understanding the connotative meanings of a word, one gains a deeper insight into whether a particular object or individual falls within its denotative scope.

questions.passage: In his exploration of how we engage with language, John Stuart Mill noted that there is a distinction between the denotation and connotation of words. The denotation of a word is its basic, dictionary definition —the straightforward umbrella term for any entity. For example, the term “human” denotes a person and can be used to refer to all human beings —Alice, Bill, and countless other individuals. To put it another way, denotation is the broad category of actual referents to which a word can be applied. Connotation, on the other hand, is more complicated as it encompasses all the <u>additional</u> attributes and contexts a word can carry that may not be part of its explicit definition. The term “human,” according to Mill, embodies characteristics such as corporeality, biological life, the ability to reason, and a specific external form, and these are what make the word “human” applicable to all the individuals. In essence, grasping the connotation of a word means having a nuanced understanding of the entity the word refers to. By understanding the connotative meanings of a word, one gains a deeper insight into whether a particular object or individual falls within its denotative scope.
